# Word-class editor: pages, page breaks, colour, tables, media, math ## Context Twyne's editor (`src/components/editor/twyne-editor.tsx`, TipTap 3.22.4 driven imperatively from Qwik) is a single continuous scrolling column. "Pages" today are a CSS illusion: `--doc-width` plus `--doc-pad-*` custom properties painted onto `.page-canvas`, with a word-count/250 "folios" estimate in the status bar. PDF export punts pagination entirely to Chrome's print engine, so what a writer sees and what they get are two unrelated layouts. The ask is to close the gap with a real word processor: true paginated canvas, manual page breaks, multi-colour highlighting, a full character/paragraph formatting suite, find & replace, page setup with headers and footers, a `/` insert menu, inline (not off-screen) note editing, discoverable keybindings, a proper image pipeline, much stronger tables, and LaTeX math. ### Three things found while exploring that change the shape of the work 1. **Strikethrough already works.** `toggleStrike()` is wired at `twyne-editor.tsx:1809`, the toolbar button is at `:2008`, active state is mirrored at `:593`. It is not missing. What *is* broken is below. 2. **Markdown export destroys all inline formatting.** `htmlToMarkdown()` (`src/utils/exchange.ts:50`) calls `stripHtml()` on its first line, then runs regexes over plain text. Bold, italic, strike, links, highlights, code — all flattened. This is almost certainly what made strikethrough look absent. Fixing it is in scope. 3. **Two live PDF-export bugs.** `wrapStandaloneHtml()` (`exchange.ts:92-197`) sets margins on both `@page` (`:129`) and `body` (`:130-139`), so every printed margin is doubled; and its `@bottom-center { content: counter(page) }` is a Paged-Media margin box Chrome does not implement, so page numbers have never rendered. The `exportPdf` doc-comment at `:519` claims otherwise and is wrong. ### Approach Six phases, each independently shippable. Phase 1 is the risky one and everything else is additive; phases 2–6 can be reordered freely. New extensions all mirror the structure and doc-comment style of `src/components/editor/extensions/mark-anchor-widgets.ts`, the existing precedent for a ProseMirror `Plugin` + `DecorationSet` in this codebase. Pure geometry is factored into DOM-free modules for `bun test`, exactly as `popover-positioning.ts` did. ### New dependencies (all verified available on npm) `@tiptap/extension-text-style@3` (TextStyleKit: Color, FontFamily, FontSize, LineHeight, BackgroundColor) · `@tiptap/extension-subscript@3` · `@tiptap/extension-superscript@3` · `@tiptap/extension-mathematics@3` + `katex@0.18` · `@tiptap/suggestion@3`. Find & Replace, table of contents, and drag handles are **TipTap Pro** — we build our own instead (each is ~150 lines against the decoration pattern already in the repo). --- ## Phase 1 — True paginated canvas The document stays **one continuous ProseMirror**. Pagination inserts invisible spacer widgets that make vertical space, and all drawing happens in a separate overlay. Nothing touches the schema, so `getHTML()`, Lix sync, comment reconciliation, and undo are all unaffected. ### The invariant Spacer heights are chosen so every page's content top lands on a uniform grid: ``` renderedTop(page k) = k * (pageH + gap) + marginTop ``` That makes the sheet paint a single `repeating-linear-gradient` (zero per-page DOM, scales to thousands of pages) and makes header/page-number positions pure arithmetic. ``` contentH = pageH − marginTop − marginBottom used_k = naturalTop(first block of page k+1) − naturalTop(first block of page k) spanned_k = 1 + max(0, ceil((used_k − contentH) / pageH)) spacer_k = spanned_k * (pageH + gap) − used_k ``` ### Why the measure→decorate→relayout loop terminates **Never read `offsetTop`.** Read only `offsetHeight` and computed `margin-top`/`margin-bottom` per block, then compute the natural stack ourselves: ``` naturalTop[i+1] = naturalTop[i] + h[i] + max(marginBottom[i], marginTop[i+1]) ``` This is a fixed point by construction: spacers don't change block widths, so they don't change `offsetHeight`. It matters concretely here — headings carry `margin-top: 2.2rem` (`global.css:321`) which collapses with the preceding paragraph's `margin-bottom`, and a spacer between them would stop that collapse. Reading `offsetTop` would oscillate ~15px at every heading break. Second guard: deep-equal the new break list and skip the dispatch if unchanged. Identify blocks by walking `state.doc` top-level children and calling `view.nodeDOM(pos)` — **not** by indexing `.ProseMirror.children`, which stray widget decorations shift. ### Read/write discipline ``` view.update() → if (docChanged || configChanged) markDirty(firstDirtyIndex) → rAF (coalesced, 90ms typing-quiet gate) READ : offsetHeight / getComputedStyle for dirty blocks only ← one forced layout PURE : paginate(metrics, geometry) WRITE : dispatch tr.setMeta(...) + onPagesChanged(count) → Qwik store ``` Per-keystroke cost is one forced layout (which the browser was doing anyway) plus microseconds of arithmetic — `paginate` is a single O(n) pass over plain numbers, ~50µs for 5,000 blocks, so there's no value in making it incremental. Full remeasure triggers: `ResizeObserver` on `.ProseMirror` (image decode, mermaid render, table column drag), `ResizeObserver` on `.page-canvas` (window resize, panel toggle, zen mode), `document.fonts` `loadingdone`, and layout-setting changes. No `IntersectionObserver` — the uniform grid makes it useless. **Scroll anchoring is mandatory.** Before dispatch, record `view.coordsAtPos(selection.head).top` relative to the scroller (`twyne-editor.tsx:2798`); after the next rAF, re-read and apply the delta to `scrollTop`. Without it the feature feels broken the first time a webfont lands. Widget spec: `key: 'pb:${k}:${round(px)}'` (stable identity — without it every keystroke recreates every spacer and the document flickers), `side: -100` (sorts before `MarkAnchorWidgets`' `side: 1`), `marks: []`, `ignoreSelection: true`. Escape hatches: `PAGINATION_MAX_BLOCKS = 20_000` / `PAGINATION_MAX_PAGES = 2_000`, past which pagination disables and falls back to continuous flow; plus a user-facing `pagination: "paginated" | "continuous"` toggle in the layout popover. ### v1 contract: blocks break atomically No interior paragraph breaks, no table row splitting. This is deliberate, not laziness: - **Widgets cannot live in ``** — the browser hoists a `
` out of a table and the spacer lands in the wrong place. The v2 fix is `Decoration.node` + `tr[data-page-break-before] > td { padding-top }`, plus changing `.tableWrapper { overflow-x: auto }` (`global.css:506`) which independently blocks fragmentation. - **Interior paragraph breaks** would break `text-align: justify` (`global.css:281`) at the split, orphan the `::first-letter` drop cap (`global.css:287`), paint `pre`/`blockquote` backgrounds straight through the page gap, and sit inside `indent.ts`'s inline `margin-left` box. Atomic paragraphs look like aggressive widow control, which is acceptable typography. Widow/orphan handling lives entirely in the pure `paginate()`: `keepWithNext` for headings (never last on a page — mirrors `break-after: avoid` in print), with a guard that drops the constraint rather than looping if a run exceeds a page. A block taller than a page starts a fresh page and overflows via `spanned_k`. Mitigate for images with `img { max-height: var(--page-content-h) }`; tag everything else `data-overflows-page` and render a legible "continues" affordance rather than pretending it's fine. **This is the fidelity ceiling of the approach, and it is the same ceiling Google Docs has.** ### Interactions verified - **`indent.ts`** — no changes. Because we read rendered `offsetHeight`, the narrower column and its extra wrapping are captured for free. Discipline: never derive heights from character counts. - **`mark-anchor-widgets.ts`** — ProseMirror unions decorations across plugins; they coexist. Drive-by fix: add `key` to its chip widget so it stops recreating DOM every keystroke. - **`remote-cursors.ts`** — the caret is `1.4em` against `1.8` line-height, so it cannot change a line box; `setRemoteCursors` dispatches with `!docChanged` so it never triggers remeasure. Pin `.remote-cursor { max-height: 1.4em }` and comment that the height is load-bearing. - **Endnote CSS counters** (`global.css:2312`) — one `.ProseMirror` means `counter-reset` is untouched. Spacers must never carry `counter-reset` or `contain`. input.new_string:
* No PDF library. The HTML export carries the writer's page setup as real
 * `@page` rules — paper size, orientation and margins — and a print engine is
 * the one renderer guaranteed to honour them. Bolting on jsPDF or html2canvas
 * would mean re-implementing pagination, and canvas-based approaches rasterise
 * the text, which loses selection, search and accessible structure.
 *
 * What the stylesheet cannot carry is the page number. `counter(page)` is
 * readable only inside an `@page` margin box, and Chrome implements neither
 * the margin-box selector nor the counter outside it — an earlier version of
 * this exporter emitted `@bottom-center { content: counter(page) }` and it
 * printed nothing, for years. A `position: fixed` header does repeat on every
 * printed page, so the running header works; the number does not, and the
 * honest fix is a second pass that runs the screen engine over the export
 * document and writes literal numbers into it.
 *
 * The trade is that the writer passes through the browser's print dialog and
 * picks "Save as PDF" there.

Done with Phase 1 and the read-aloud fix. Let me summarize.

**Pagination — true paginated canvas (Phase 1, complete and verified)**

The document stays one continuous ProseMirror; nothing touches the schema, so `getHTML()`, the Lix mirror, comment reconciliation and undo are unaffected. Invisible spacer widgets make the page gaps, sized so every page's content top lands on a uniform grid (`k × (pageH + gap)`), which makes the sheets, headers and page numbers pure arithmetic.

The design decision that carries it: **the engine never reads `offsetTop`**. It reads only `offsetHeight` and computed margins and reconstructs the stack itself, so its own spacers can't change its own inputs — the measure→decorate→relayout loop is a fixed point by construction rather than by tuning. That matters concretely here: your headings carry `margin-top: 2.2rem` which collapses with the preceding paragraph, and an `offsetTop`-based engine would oscillate ~15px at every heading forever.

New: `pagination-geometry.ts` (pure, 39 tests), `extensions/pagination.ts`, `extensions/page-break-node.ts`, `page-chrome.tsx`, `utils/css-units.ts`. Paper size (Letter/A4/Legal), orientation, and a paginated/continuous toggle are in the layout popover; all four `LayoutSettings` fields are optional so folios saved before today still open on Letter portrait.

Three real bugs the tests caught, not the plan:
- A block after a manual page break kept its top margin and landed 20px below the page top. CSS truncates margins at a fragmentation boundary; the engine now does too.
- The canvas shrank with the viewport, so narrowing the window changed the page count from 5 to 7. A sheet is a physical size — it now keeps its width and the area around it scrolls.
- The absolutely-positioned sheets added no height, so a partly-full last page was clipped where the prose stopped.

`Mod-Enter` was already bound twice (hard break via StarterKit, `exitCode` in `@tiptap/core`); the page break takes it at priority 200 but yields inside a code block, since escaping one has no other keystroke.

**Export/print** — fixed the doubled margins (`@page` *and* `body` both set them), deleted the `@bottom-center` rule that has never rendered in Chrome, pinned `html { font-size: 16px }` so rem→inch conversion is exact, and mirrored the engine's atomic-block and keep-with-next decisions into the print stylesheet. The `exportPdf` doc-comment claiming page numbers worked is corrected.

**Read aloud** — you were right that it was broken. `getCachedAiSettings()` and `withPersonaVoice()` were called *outside* the try block and before `setState("loading")`, so on a browser with no AI settings `speak()` rejected with the UI still showing idle: press, nothing, ever. Now the whole path is inside the try, and there's a real transport — play/pause/resume, stop, a seek slider with mm:ss, and the error rendered inline. Pausing holds the position instead of discarding it (restarting a five-minute reading to answer the door is not a feature). `SpeakButton` in the popovers learned the same pause semantics.

**Verification:** 13 Playwright tests pass (including "no block straddles a sheet boundary" and a no-thrash assertion that 50 keystrokes cause ≤4 measurement passes), 39 geometry unit tests, typecheck clean, lint clean apart from 2 pre-existing warnings in `routes/downloads/`.
